The Problem

The software gap that slows businesses down.

Many businesses do not need a huge engineering department. They need a practical software partner who can turn unclear ideas, broken workflows, and unfinished products into tools that actually work.

The risk is not just bad code. It is unclear scope, silent weeks, missed launches, messy handoff, and software nobody can maintain after the developer leaves.

Who This Is For

Is this you?

  • ✓ You have an idea, MVP, or internal tool that needs to become real software.
  • ✓ Your current website does not clearly explain your offer or convert visitors.
  • ✓ Your existing app is buggy, unfinished, slow, or hard to maintain.
  • ✓ You need dashboards, automations, APIs, or AI tools to reduce manual work.
  • ✓ You want clear communication, written scope, and clean handoff.

Most CodeVault clients are founders, small teams, operators, and businesses that need reliable product development without hiring a full-time engineering team.

Not The Right Fit If
  • × You only want the cheapest possible developer.
  • × You want to start without clear goals or feedback.
  • × You expect a full product overnight without scope.
  • × You do not want to review or test the work.
  • × You want a huge agency layer instead of a focused build partner.

AI In The Workflow

AI speeds up the build. Judgment still owns the result.

CodeVault uses AI where it helps: planning, debugging, refactoring, documentation, repetitive implementation, and review. But architecture, product decisions, security, user experience, and final quality control stay human.

The goal is not AI decoration. The goal is useful software shipped with less waste.

Questions

Before we work together.

How much does a project cost? +

It depends on scope, timeline, and complexity. A landing page is usually smaller than an MVP or product rescue. The first call is used to understand the work and suggest the right engagement.

How long does a landing page take? +

Most focused landing pages can be completed in one to two weeks if the offer, content direction, and feedback are clear.

How long does an MVP take? +

MVP timelines depend on features, integrations, and quality expectations. CodeVault starts by defining the smallest useful version that can be launched and tested.

Can you work with my existing codebase? +

Yes. For existing projects, the first step is usually an audit to understand the structure, bugs, risks, and best path forward.

Can you design and build? +

Yes. CodeVault can handle structure, UI direction, frontend, backend, integrations, and deployment support depending on the project.

Can you deploy the project? +

Yes. Deployment support can include hosting setup, environment variables, domains, production checks, and handoff notes.

Can you build mobile apps? +

Yes. CodeVault can build mobile apps using React Native, especially for MVPs, internal tools, and product ideas that need both iOS and Android coverage.

Can you add AI features? +

Yes, when AI actually helps the product. This can include AI writing, summarization, automation, classification, assistants, or workflow acceleration.

What do you need from me to start? +

A clear idea of the problem, target users, deadline, budget range, examples you like, and any existing assets or code.

Do you offer ongoing support? +

Yes. After launch, CodeVault can continue with fixes, improvements, new features, and product support through a monthly engagement.
